• Flooding has become more frequent along much of the U.S. coastline since the 1950s. Some areas have experienced a dramatic acceleration, particularly along the East and Gulf coasts.
  • Coastal flooding is expected to continue to increase at all the locations studied. The lower sea level rise scenario shown here is closest to what climate modeling suggests will occur in the intermediate emissions scenario used in other pairings. The higher scenario is most closely linked to the very high emissions scenario used in other pairings. Both scenarios show flooding continuing to increase. At some cities, flood conditions that occur a few times per year now could become a near-daily norm by the end of this century.
